question.problem: What is the domain of the function $f(x)=-3\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{x}{6}-\frac{\pi }{3})?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
question.worked_solution:
The domain of $y=\operatorname{csc}⁡x$ consists of all values where $\operatorname{sin}⁡x\ne 0,$ and is given by the expression

$$
x\ne n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the domain of $-3\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{x}{6}-\frac{\pi }{3}),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $(\frac{x}{6}-\frac{\pi }{3}).$ This gives

$$
\frac{x}{6}-\frac{\pi }{3}\ne n\pi .
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{6}-\frac{\pi }{3} & \ne n\pi  \\ \frac{x}{6} & \ne \frac{\pi }{3}+n\pi  \\ x & \ne \frac{6\pi }{3}+6n\pi  \\ x & \ne 2\pi +6n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the domain of the function is $x\ne 2\pi +6n\pi ,$ where $n$ is an integer.
